metadata.description: The @dereekb/trello/cli LIBRARY entry (rollup, inferred from rollup.config.cjs): compiles into dist/packages/trello/cli and is named by the parent's `./cli` export. An explicit edge to trello:build-base, NOT `^build`: `^build` would resolve to trello:build, which depends on this very target -- a hard cycle. trello-node is an in-family sibling entry (like zoho-cli -> zoho-nestjs), so its `build-base` is the edge too, and package.json lists it as a peer. dbx-cli and util are other families, so their ROOT `build` is the edge (the finalized copy TypeScript resolves `exports` against). package.json also lists dbx-cli's typed peers (date, firebase, model, oauth-resource, rxjs) with no source usage, as dbx-cli/test does: dbx-cli's .d.ts files import them, and an undeclared one resolves to its SOURCE through the tsconfig paths, which fails the rollup declaration pass with TS6059 (outside rootDir). dbx-cli:build already builds them. The parent's `build` aggregates this target, so the entry point has no `build` of its own.

The trello-cli EXECUTABLE (the `trello-cli` bin of @dereekb/trello): src/main.ts bundled with the @dereekb/* sources inlined and npm packages left external, the package refs embedded through the `.md` text loader. It writes its own directory (dist/packages/trello/bin), so each dist directory has one writer. The edge to trello:build-base orders it after the parent's rollup, which clears dist/packages/trello.

trello.cli.bundle.spec.ts runs the BUILT binary (dist/packages/trello/bin/index.js) and reads the parent's dist package.json / refs, so both entry points are built first. The nx default test.dependsOn ["build"] names a target this entry point does not have (see build-base) and is skipped silently.
